title: Storefront API
oneLiner: TypeScript store API on Express and PostgreSQL—catalog, cart-shaped reads, and typed boundaries for a future storefront client.
impactMetric: Typed modules · Postgres as source of truth

problem.heading: Problem
problem.description: Store demos often start as unbounded JSON blobs. I needed a small but honest commerce backend: normalized product data, predictable query patterns, and TypeScript modules that another engineer could extend without reading the whole repo twice.

myRole.heading: My role
myRole.description: Designed the schema and migrations mindset, implemented Express routes with validation, centralized error shapes, and documented environment setup so the API could run locally against Dockerized Postgres.

solution.heading: Solution
solution.description: Storefront API layers repositories over SQL, keeps DTOs explicit at boundaries, and avoids ORM magic in favor of readable queries for catalog and inventory paths that a storefront would actually call.

impact.heading: Impact
metrics: 🧱 Clean split: HTTP layer, helpers, and Postgres access
📄 README-first onboarding for contributors and walkthroughs
impact.description: Backend sample work that foregrounds contracts and data modeling—the half of the stack customers never see but teams feel every day.
